messages.content: أرغب في معرفة توقعات الطقس لمدينة نيويورك خلال الأسبوع القادم. هل يمكنك استرداد بيانات الطقس لخط العرض 40.7128 وخط الطول -74.0060؟

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants weather forecast for New York City for next week. We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate parameters. The function signature includes url, headers optional, timeout optional, params including latitude, longitude, elevation optional, allow_redirects optional, auth optional, cert optional, cookies optional, proxies optional, stream optional, verify optional.

We need to construct a request to Open-Meteo API. The typical endpoint for forecast is "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to pass latitude=40.7128, longitude=-74.0060. Also we might want to specify daily parameters like temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, etc. But the user didn't specify which parameters. We can just fetch default forecast. But maybe we should ask clarifying question? The user specifically says "توقعات الطقس لمدينة نيويورك خلال الأسبوع القادم" meaning "weather forecast for New York City for next week." So we should provide daily forecast for next 7 days. We can request daily parameters: temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, windspeed_10m_max, windgusts_10m_max, shortwave_radiation_sum, uv_index_max, sunrise, sunset. But we can keep it simple: daily temperature max/min, precipitation sum, wind speed max, etc.

Open-Meteo API supports daily parameters via "daily" query param. For example: daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,windspeed_10m_max,windgusts_10m_max,shortwave_radiation_sum,uv_index_max,sunrise,sunset. Also we can set timezone=America/New_York. And we can set start_date and end_date. For next week, we can set start_date as tomorrow's date, end_date as 7 days later. But we don't have date calculation tool. We can approximate: we can use today's date? But we don't know current date. We could ask clarifying question about date. But we can also just request forecast for next 7 days starting from today. The API will return forecast for next 7 days by default if we don't specify start_date. Actually the API returns forecast for next 7 days by default if we don't specify start_date. But we can specify "forecast_days=7" parameter. The API supports "forecast_days" param. So we can set forecast_days=7. That will give us 7 days forecast.

Thus we can call:

requests_get({
  url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  params: {
    latitude: 40.7128,
    longitude: -74.0060,
    daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,windspeed_10m_max,windgusts_10m_max,shortwave_radiation_sum,uv_index_max,sunrise,sunset",
    timezone: "America/New_York",
    forecast_days: 7
  }
})

We don't need other optional fields. We'll set default headers. So we call the function.
